title: Languages going quiet
hook: About 7,000 languages, and many have only a few speakers left.
notes: Ethnologue (2024): ≈ 7,160 living languages, ≈ 44% endangered; half the world speaks one of ≈ 23 languages. Language counts per country approximate.

scenes.title: Where languages live
scenes.text: Papua New Guinea alone has around 840 languages. Indonesia, Nigeria and India each have hundreds. Half of humanity speaks one of just 23 languages.

scenes.title: The last speaker
scenes.text: In 2022, Cristina Calderón died in Puerto Williams, Chile. She was the last native speaker of Yaghan, the language of people who lived at the southern tip of the Americas.

scenes.title: Livonian
scenes.text: In 2013, Grizelda Kristiņa, the last native speaker of Livonian from the Latvian coast, died at 103. A small community still learns it today.

scenes.title: Coming back
scenes.text: Languages can return. Manx lost its last native speaker in 1974 and now has a primary school. Hawaiian, once nearly gone, is taught from preschool to university. Ainu in Japan is being revived too.
